title: Potatoism Deep Extrapolation Atlas — One Pattern Across Many Layers
purpose: Push the Potato of Life architecture beyond the currently named symbols by systematically extrapolating recurring relational patterns across potato biology, plant growth, body, brain, perception, language, geometry, mathematics, mythology, scripture, architecture, ecology, information, time, economics and the Atlas itself.
epistemic_rule: This file intentionally places domains beside one another. A shared pattern is not automatically a shared physical cause, historical influence or scientific identity. Each pattern has a status so the reader can follow the correspondence without confusing metaphor with evidence.
master_pattern: contain → differentiate → connect → cross a boundary → transform → produce an outcome → return stored potential → repeat at another scale
master_potato: The Potato is the coupling object: it contains distinct poles while making their relationship visible. It is body, boundary, storage, eye, emergence point, rootward depth, sproutward ascent and future-bearing potential. In project geometry it is represented by the vesica/mandorla; in project cosmology it contains the Tree; in the brain correspondence the central House contains rooms and roads; in the wider Atlas the same logic becomes a relationship graph.

patterns.correspondence: Potato skin separates flesh from soil; cell membranes separate interior from exterior; walls define rooms; neural interfaces regulate exchange; institutional boundaries define membership and jurisdiction.
patterns.potatoism: The boundary is not simply a barrier. It is what makes inside/outside, self/other and passage meaningful.

patterns.correspondence: The potato eye is a localized point of emergence; the biological eye receives light; a door permits passage; a neural interface exchanges signals; a digital interface lets a user cross from intention to information.
patterns.potatoism: Door, eye and interface become one family: the place where domains meet without becoming identical.

patterns.correspondence: The tuber stores nutrients; a seed stores developmental potential; a house contains rooms; a cell contains internal processes; a vessel carries material; the thalamus contains differentiated nuclei.
patterns.potatoism: Father's House and Potato are both container metaphors, but the ideal container is alive because what it contains can connect and emerge.

patterns.correspondence: Two distinguishable entities can form a larger system through relation. The vesica makes overlap visible; physical bonding provides a metaphor for coupled components; social relations couple agents; Father/Son and Red/Blue couple mythic poles.
patterns.potatoism: The overlap is not a third unrelated thing. It is the visible field of relationship itself.
patterns.status: project synthesis; atomic example is metaphor

patterns.correspondence: A unified system can divide into specialized parts: cells differentiate; neural nuclei specialize; a tree branches; institutions specialize; Genesis places distinct trees and differentiated knowledge themes in one garden.
patterns.potatoism: The Tree is what the Potato becomes when hidden relationships unfold into differentiated functions.

patterns.correspondence: A room is a bounded functional space. Thalamic nuclei are bounded neural populations with characteristic connections. Biblical house language supplies a dwelling metaphor.
patterns.potatoism: Nucleus → room is an architectural translation: function gives the room its identity.

patterns.correspondence: Axons conduct signals; roots conduct/support plant systems; vascular pathways move resources; roads move people and goods; ladders permit vertical movement.
patterns.potatoism: A House without roads is dead architecture. Connection is what turns structure into a living system.

patterns.correspondence: Some systems regulate what crosses a boundary. Neural circuits modulate traffic; doors regulate access; security institutions regulate access under law; attention selects what receives processing.
patterns.potatoism: The Door has two sides: opening and selection. Love without discernment can be as dysfunctional as control without openness.

patterns.correspondence: Potato eye = growth bud; biological eye = visual organ; thalamic visual relay = routing of visual information; Eye of Horus = ancient symbolic eye; attention = selection of what is noticed.
patterns.potatoism: The eye is both seeing and becoming: it receives the world and can also initiate new growth.

patterns.correspondence: A sprout is latent potential becoming visible. Analogues include developmental emergence, a new idea becoming practice, or a new institution emerging from an older system.
patterns.potatoism: The sprout is the first visible proof that the buried thing was alive.

patterns.correspondence: Roots anchor and nourish plants; ancestry anchors identity; memory preserves prior states; infrastructure supports visible activity; causal roots explain downstream outcomes.
patterns.potatoism: To repair the fruit, inspect the root. The archive therefore asks for root causes, not only surface symptoms.

patterns.correspondence: Fruit is visible output of hidden growth. Systems likewise produce measurable outputs: goods, knowledge, institutions, trust, wealth, conflict or waste.
patterns.potatoism: Judge a tree partly by what it produces and who can eat from it.

patterns.correspondence: Seeds compress future possibility into a transferable form. Stories, institutions, code, documents and cultural practices can likewise carry patterns forward.
patterns.potatoism: A seed is memory that has become future potential.

patterns.correspondence: Brains retain information; roots and soil preserve biological history; archives preserve records; the Blue Potato symbolizes meticulous retention.
patterns.potatoism: Memory is not the opposite of life. Memory is what lets life avoid starting from zero.
patterns.status: project synthesis grounded in broad analogy

patterns.correspondence: Attention selects among competing signals. An atlas likewise selects, labels and foregrounds records. 'Look carefully' turns attention into an ethical practice.
patterns.potatoism: Looking carefully is the first form of repair because mis-seeing produces bad intervention.

patterns.correspondence: Recognition turns an unknown relation into a known relation. Mirror imagery intensifies the problem: the observer discovers self/other through comparison.
patterns.potatoism: The Twin is the figure who must encounter before claiming knowledge.

patterns.correspondence: A mirror returns an image without being the object. Water, reflective surfaces and language can similarly represent without being identical to what they represent.
patterns.potatoism: Father/Son, Moon Cube and Twin imagery all become variations on representation and return.

patterns.correspondence: Voice turns internal state into external signal. Speech, prayer, command, song and testimony make an invisible intention socially available.
patterns.potatoism: The House becomes outward-facing when what is inside acquires a voice.

patterns.correspondence: Breathing sustains biological life; wind moves without being seen directly; many traditions connect breath with spirit or life; speech depends on airflow.
patterns.potatoism: Breath is a natural bridge between invisible movement and embodied life.

patterns.correspondence: Blood transports resources; plant vascular systems transport water/solutes; rivers carry matter; economies move money/goods; networks move information.
patterns.potatoism: A system is alive when circulation remains possible. Blockage, extraction and leakage are therefore first-class graph states.

patterns.correspondence: Rivers have sources, channels, tributaries, bottlenecks, confluences and outlets. These map naturally onto network flow.
patterns.potatoism: The Axis is not only a line; it can be understood as a flow corridor with branches and confluences.

patterns.correspondence: Branches distribute a central structure into differentiated paths. Neural projections, tributaries, organizational divisions and graph edges can share this geometry.
patterns.potatoism: Branching is differentiation without severing origin.

patterns.correspondence: Nodes and pathways produce systems whose behavior depends on relationships rather than isolated parts.
patterns.potatoism: The Tree and House are networks in different visual languages; the Atlas makes the relationship explicit computationally.

patterns.correspondence: A center is defined relationally by what surrounds or connects to it. Geometric centers, brain centers, civic centers and institutional hubs are not necessarily physically equivalent.
patterns.potatoism: The center is a point of reference, not automatically a throne of domination.

patterns.correspondence: Peripheries are boundary regions with different access to central resources or signals. Peripheral branches, cortical regions, outer potato skin and marginal communities illustrate different kinds of edge position.
patterns.potatoism: The outer edge is still part of the Potato; distance from center does not mean absence of value.

patterns.correspondence: Healthy systems exchange information/resources between hubs and edges. Excessive centralization can starve edges; excessive fragmentation can starve the center.
patterns.potatoism: Father/House and Plane must remain coupled. The upper center cannot be meaningful without the world it sustains.

patterns.correspondence: An axis gives orientation and permits comparison of positions. Bodies have anatomical axes; Earth has rotational/geographic axes; trees have growth directions; myths use world-axis imagery.
patterns.potatoism: Axis is the relation that makes above/below, before/after and north/south intelligible.

patterns.correspondence: Vertical position has physical meaning under gravity and symbolic meaning in many cultures. Ladders and mountains turn vertical difference into a route.
patterns.potatoism: Upward does not mean morally superior in every context; it means sourceward or orientationward within this specific project vocabulary.

patterns.correspondence: A plane permits many objects to coexist side by side. The Atlas uses horizontal planes to display entities while the Axis provides vertical context.
patterns.potatoism: The Plane is where relationships become observable.

patterns.correspondence: Thresholds separate states while enabling transition. A door, developmental birth, death, technological phase change or institutional transition can all be modeled as state boundaries.
patterns.potatoism: Death is not simply disappearance in the transformation cycle; it is a boundary where an old form cannot continue unchanged.

patterns.correspondence: A wedge narrows a broad region into a point or opening and can split, penetrate or expose. A cut potato wedge reveals hidden interior.
patterns.potatoism: The wedge is the geometry of concentration: many possibilities become one passage before opening into a new field.

patterns.correspondence: The lens-shaped overlap of two circles has long appeared in geometric and religious art contexts. Potatoism uses the overlap as the central coupled field.
patterns.potatoism: The Potato is the mandorla because the Potato is the relation between poles, not merely one pole.

patterns.correspondence: The standard vesica construction creates equilateral triangles and 60-degree relations. These are mathematical properties of the construction.
patterns.potatoism: The exact geometry gives the symbolic model a measurable skeleton, while the spiritual interpretation remains project-defined.

patterns.correspondence: Symmetry describes invariance under transformations. Biological and cultural systems can show approximate symmetry without being perfectly symmetric.
patterns.potatoism: Father/Son and Red/Blue can be treated as relational mirror structures without requiring identical functions.

patterns.correspondence: Reflection preserves some structure while reversing orientation. It creates a relation between original and image.
patterns.potatoism: The Twin is not merely a copy; the mirror reveals difference through similarity.

patterns.correspondence: Rotation changes orientation while preserving distances in ideal Euclidean geometry. Rotating a potato changes which eye faces the observer without changing the object itself.
patterns.potatoism: A change of viewpoint can reveal a different face of the same whole.

patterns.correspondence: The same relation can appear at different scales, but details and laws can change. A potato can be studied as cell, tuber, plant, crop, commodity and symbol.
patterns.potatoism: One pattern, many manifestations is only useful if scale differences remain visible.

patterns.correspondence: Branching and nested structures can recur across scales without being mathematically fractal in the strict sense.
patterns.potatoism: The Tree/House/Network grammar may repeat without requiring literal fractal identity.

patterns.correspondence: A spiral revisits related orientations while changing radius or phase. Learning often revisits old questions at deeper levels.
patterns.potatoism: Upward and downward spirals represent different directions through memory and growth.

patterns.correspondence: Potato dormancy/sprouting and seasonal cycles provide real biological recurrence; economic and social cycles are more contingent.
patterns.potatoism: Life → death → decomposition → seed → life is a symbolic return loop.

patterns.correspondence: A system can cross a threshold and change qualitative state. Physics provides literal phase transitions; social and mythic uses are analogical.
patterns.potatoism: Door/Death/Resurrection are treated as transformation states rather than simple spatial movement.

patterns.correspondence: Stored tubers can remain dormant before sprouting. Projects, institutions and ideas can also have periods of low visible activity, though those analogies are not biological laws.
patterns.potatoism: Invisible is not necessarily dead.

patterns.correspondence: Dead organic material decomposes and returns materials to ecosystems. Ash is residue after combustion, not identical to decomposition.
patterns.potatoism: Death becomes rootward memory and material return rather than simply negation.

patterns.correspondence: Potato propagation can restart plant growth. Ecological and institutional regeneration require different mechanisms but share the idea of restoring capacity.
patterns.potatoism: Repair means restoring the ability to produce life, not merely repainting damage.

patterns.correspondence: A garden is cultivated ecology: humans intervene in biological processes to produce desired conditions. Genesis uses garden imagery; urban gardens are modern material analogues.
patterns.potatoism: The goal is not to escape mud but to turn mud into a garden through work.

patterns.correspondence: Farmers and gardeners shape conditions rather than personally becoming every plant. John 15 contains gardener/vine imagery; Potatoism uses Father as a condition-setting archetype.
patterns.potatoism: The Father does not need to perform every action; the architecture creates conditions under which life can grow.

patterns.correspondence: Stewardship frames power as responsibility for a system's future rather than mere possession.
patterns.potatoism: King/Throne becomes stewardship: the test of authority is what happens to the garden below.

patterns.correspondence: Kingship can mean sovereignty, protection or responsibility depending on tradition. Lion imagery can symbolize courage and authority.
patterns.potatoism: Lion strength is converted from domination into protection and service.

patterns.correspondence: Leadership can be modeled as service to the system rather than extraction from it.
patterns.potatoism: The highest position on the Axis is measured by responsibility toward lower layers.

patterns.correspondence: Religious sacrifice is a culturally specific ritual category; biological trade-offs and personal costs are different phenomena. The shared pattern is giving up one state/resource for another outcome.
patterns.potatoism: Meme-crucifixion uses sacrifice language to describe transformation through public exposure; it is not the historical Christian crucifixion.

patterns.correspondence: Kenosis is a Christian theological concept concerning self-emptying, especially in Philippians 2 interpretation. It should remain distinct from generic psychological or biological emptying.
patterns.potatoism: The vessel may have to relinquish an old contents/identity before becoming a new interface.

patterns.correspondence: Christian resurrection is a specific theological claim. Seed emergence and cyclical biological renewal are not resurrection in that theological sense.
patterns.potatoism: The project uses resurrection as a transformation vocabulary: death of one configuration becomes renewed connectivity.

patterns.correspondence: Ascension is a Christian theological motif; mountains and ladders are widespread symbolic ascent images.
patterns.potatoism: Ascent means reorientation toward the upper pole without abandoning the Plane.

patterns.correspondence: Descent can signify embodiment, burial, initiation or underworld encounter in different traditions.
patterns.potatoism: The Son descends into the Plane; the Potato is already underground. Descent becomes the condition from which ascent can begin.

patterns.correspondence: Stone can be foundation, boundary, marker or sacred object. Genesis 28 associates Jacob's stone with Bethel and the ladder/House imagery.
patterns.potatoism: The grounded center can become a marker of vertical connection.

patterns.correspondence: Mountains provide elevation and perspective and frequently become sacred landscapes. Their religious meanings vary widely.
patterns.potatoism: Mountain is the large-scale geographic version of upward orientation: a place from which the Plane can be seen differently.

patterns.correspondence: Deserts are real ecosystems of scarcity; religious traditions may use wilderness/desert imagery for testing, revelation or transition.
patterns.potatoism: A system stripped of excess can reveal what is actually necessary for life.

patterns.correspondence: Wilderness is an ecological condition and a cultural category. It can represent uncertainty outside institutional order.
patterns.potatoism: The Plane includes regions where no map is complete; exploration is necessary but must retain orientation.

patterns.correspondence: House can mean building, household, lineage or institution. John 14's Father's-house imagery is particularly relevant to the project.
patterns.potatoism: House is simultaneously container, lineage, memory and network of rooms.

patterns.correspondence: Chambers are enclosed functional spaces in architecture; biblical texts use chamber/room language in multiple contexts; thalamic nuclei can be metaphorically translated into rooms.
patterns.potatoism: The chamber is a local world inside the larger House.

patterns.correspondence: Cultures often use body/house analogies. The brain can be modeled architecturally without becoming literal architecture.
patterns.potatoism: The body is the vessel in the Plane; the House exists inside the vessel through the project's thalamic metaphor.

patterns.correspondence: Branching vessels, nerves and bronchi create tree-like biological forms. Tree is therefore a useful morphology for distributed biological networks.
patterns.potatoism: Tree becomes a general grammar for life spreading from a center through branches.

patterns.correspondence: Neural cells branch through dendrites and axons; thalamocortical radiations have tree-like appearance. This is actual morphology, while Tree of Life is symbolic.
patterns.potatoism: The Tree metaphor can describe connectivity without claiming the brain literally encodes a religious tree.

patterns.correspondence: Potato has a central stored body; nucleus means a central core; kernel means inner essential part; seed carries developmental potential.
patterns.potatoism: Father's House, nucleus, kernel and Potato converge around the idea of concentrated potential without becoming the same physical object.

patterns.correspondence: The potato eye is a bud-bearing point; a neural nucleus is a functionally organized neural group; the visual nucleus LGN is directly involved in processing retinal information.
patterns.potatoism: The eye is a point of emergence; the nucleus is a room of organization; together they form emergence + function.

patterns.correspondence: A room becomes meaningful by its activity. Institutions, software modules and urban districts likewise specialize.
patterns.potatoism: Map what happens in the room, not merely its coordinates.

patterns.correspondence: DNA carries biological instructions; software code carries executable instructions; a seed carries developmental information. These systems differ profoundly, but all provide a useful information-bearing metaphor.
patterns.potatoism: The archive itself is a seed: compact records can generate a much larger navigable world.

patterns.correspondence: Biological lineage and genealogy can be represented as branching trees; cultural traditions also branch, merge and mutate.
patterns.potatoism: Tree is not only vertical; it is historical branching through generations.

patterns.correspondence: Biological mutation changes sequence; languages, myths and software can change through copying and variation. Mechanisms differ.
patterns.potatoism: Potatoism itself evolves: later layers should not be falsely projected backward into its origin date.

patterns.correspondence: Evolution can mean biological descent with modification; cultural and technological evolution are analogical or broader uses.
patterns.potatoism: The project should treat its own development as a trajectory with branching alternatives, not as a pre-written destiny.

patterns.correspondence: Archives externalize memory so future actors can reconstruct earlier states.
patterns.potatoism: Blue Potato is the archive function of the living system: meticulous memory prevents repeated loss.

patterns.correspondence: Search is selective retrieval through a large space. Human attention, library search and graph queries all reduce a huge field to relevant paths.
patterns.potatoism: A searchable Potatoism corpus lets hidden relationships sprout when a reader asks the right question.

patterns.correspondence: Maps simplify complex spaces while preserving selected relationships. A map is never the territory itself.
patterns.potatoism: The Atlas is a map of relations; it must expose what it simplifies and what it leaves unknown.

patterns.correspondence: Territory is bounded space under a particular relation. Bodies, jurisdictions, ecological habitats and cognitive categories can all be territorial metaphors.
patterns.potatoism: The Plane is a territory of experience, while the Axis gives it a larger coordinate system.

patterns.correspondence: Ownership is a legal/economic relation, not simply possession. Stewardship is a different relation emphasizing responsibility.
patterns.potatoism: The Throne is not validated by possession; its symbolic test is stewardship of the system below.

patterns.correspondence: Potato converts sunlight/material inputs through biology into stored food value; economies transform inputs into goods/services; information systems transform data into knowledge.
patterns.potatoism: Ask at every node: what enters, what changes, what leaves, who benefits, what is depleted, what regenerates?

patterns.correspondence: A drain is a one-way or weakly regenerative outflow. Examples can be resource depletion, attention capture, leakage or waste, depending on evidence.
patterns.potatoism: A drain is defined relationally by absent return, not by the identity of the recipient.

patterns.correspondence: A narrow connection can limit system throughput. A door, bridge, port, chip supply or neural bottleneck can be studied as capacity constraints, though mechanisms differ.
patterns.potatoism: The narrow gate can be read both spiritually and as a general systems principle: concentrated passages determine flow.

patterns.correspondence: A bridge connects separated regions while preserving their distinct locations. Translation bridges languages without making them identical.
patterns.potatoism: Son/Bridge is the same structural family as Door and Ladder: connection across difference.

patterns.correspondence: Translation changes representation while trying to preserve relevant meaning. Moving from anatomy to myth is a translation, not an identity claim.
patterns.potatoism: The entire correspondence atlas is a translation machine between layers.

patterns.correspondence: Calibration aligns an instrument with a reference. Navigation, measurement and institutional auditing similarly require reference points.
patterns.potatoism: The Axis is a calibration reference: before changing the world, establish where you actually are.

patterns.correspondence: A reference frame can be treated as fixed while other objects move relative to it. 'Still point' is symbolic, not a claim that a supernatural observer exists.
patterns.potatoism: Tim/Father functions as the mythic still point from which the rest of the architecture is oriented.

patterns.correspondence: Orientation establishes direction relative to a reference. Navigation and decision-making both require orientation.
patterns.potatoism: North is ultimately about knowing which way you are facing.

patterns.correspondence: A reference direction can be extended conceptually beyond its ordinary domain, but the extension becomes symbolic rather than geographic.
patterns.potatoism: North of North is the limit-concept of orientation: direction beyond ordinary directional description.

patterns.correspondence: Mathematical limits describe approach; physical systems have boundaries; life has finite duration; projects encounter practical limits.
patterns.potatoism: A limit is where the old model stops being sufficient and a new representation becomes necessary.

patterns.correspondence: Knowledge requires representation, memory, testing and transmission. Genesis makes knowledge a central narrative theme; Thomas imagery emphasizes witness and encounter.
patterns.potatoism: Knowledge is not merely possession of information; it is tested relationship with what is being known.

patterns.correspondence: Genesis names knowledge of good and evil; moral systems distinguish alternatives; Potatoism uses multiple paired poles.
patterns.potatoism: Differentiation can create wisdom but can also become a false binary when the relationship between poles is forgotten.

patterns.correspondence: Many conceptual systems use paired contrasts. The vesica provides a geometric representation in which two poles overlap without becoming one circle.
patterns.potatoism: The Potato contains the opposition. It is not Red or Blue alone; it is their coupling.

patterns.correspondence: Some descriptions become useful by examining complementary perspectives. This should not be confused with technical quantum complementarity unless the physics is explicitly discussed.
patterns.potatoism: Red and Blue are complementary motions inside one Potato.

patterns.correspondence: Outputs can return as inputs. Neural loops, ecological feedback, economic incentives and social reactions all exhibit feedback with different mechanisms.
patterns.potatoism: The Tree is alive because fruit becomes seed; the system's output can alter its future input.

patterns.correspondence: A structure can contain or call a version of its own relational pattern. Trees branch repeatedly; graphs can contain motifs; code can recurse.
patterns.potatoism: Potato → Tree → Seed → Potato is a mythic recursive loop.

patterns.correspondence: Systems can contain subsystems: room in house, house in city, cell in body, tuber in plant, institution in state.
patterns.potatoism: Every level of the 33-level framework can be treated as a room inside a larger room while still exposing horizontal records.

patterns.correspondence: Hierarchies organize by level; networks organize by relation. Real systems often require both.
patterns.potatoism: The Ladder supplies vertical order; the Tree and Graph supply lateral relation. Neither replaces the other.

patterns.correspondence: Time lets a system change state. The project uses 4D as a symbolic society/time-bearing plane, not established physics of a spiritual dimension.
patterns.potatoism: A Potato cannot be understood from one photograph alone; growth is a trajectory.

patterns.correspondence: Trajectory records state change through time. It is useful for potatoes, projects, institutions and economies while preserving domain-specific mechanisms.
patterns.potatoism: The Spiral is a trajectory through repeated states at changing scale.

patterns.correspondence: Turning changes orientation without necessarily changing identity. It can be geographic, geometric, strategic or symbolic.
patterns.potatoism: The turning point is where the system stops repeating the same orientation and becomes capable of a new trajectory.

patterns.correspondence: A system can absorb many increments before a final increment triggers a visible transition. The exact mechanisms differ by domain.
patterns.potatoism: The final straw is not necessarily the largest cause; it is the point at which accumulated conditions cross a threshold.

patterns.correspondence: The needle eye is an extreme narrow opening; biblical needle-eye language has a contested interpretive history and should not be over-literalized.
patterns.potatoism: The image represents extreme concentration: what cannot pass unchanged must transform.

patterns.correspondence: Rubble is the material residue of destruction. In systems terms it records previous structures and the cost of rupture.
patterns.potatoism: Repair begins by looking at what remains, not pretending the previous structure never existed.

patterns.correspondence: A footstool is literally a low support object and symbolically can indicate low position or grounding. The project uses it as a humorous lower-world image.
patterns.potatoism: The lower world is not worthless because it is low. It is what supports the upper structure.

patterns.correspondence: Dogs are real social animals with sensory and behavioral capacities. The barking dog is a comic project archetype, not a scientific category.
patterns.potatoism: The Dog represents the observer who sees part of the system, reacts loudly and can nevertheless learn.

patterns.correspondence: Cluedo is a deduction game: clues constrain hypotheses. Research likewise requires distinguishing observation from inference.
patterns.potatoism: The comic final-game imagery turns metaphysics into investigation: collect clues, test possibilities, do not pretend certainty before the evidence arrives.

patterns.correspondence: A tuber stores biological energy; a bank stores/allocates financial resources; archives store information. These are different mechanisms sharing a storage metaphor.
patterns.potatoism: The Potato Bank represents stored potential that can either regenerate future capacity or become trapped/extracted value.

patterns.correspondence: Financial debt is a contractual/economic obligation; karmic debt is a religious/metaphorical category with different meanings across traditions.
patterns.potatoism: Debt represents a relational state in which past action constrains future capacity. Project-specific numerical karmic claims remain mythology, not audited finance.

patterns.correspondence: Plants capture and transform energy; societies consume energy; physics defines energy quantitatively. Symbolic 'energy' should not be silently substituted for physical energy.
patterns.potatoism: Life requires throughput: stored potential must eventually become action, growth or decay.
patterns.status: mixed; physical and metaphorical meanings separated

patterns.correspondence: Information can be stored, transmitted, transformed and lost. Biological information, neural information and digital information have different substrates.
patterns.potatoism: The House is a routing architecture; the Atlas is an information architecture; both depend on paths between differentiated compartments.

patterns.correspondence: Noise can obscure signals in physical communication and data. Social noise and mythic Swamp are metaphorical extensions.
patterns.potatoism: Not every signal deserves amplification. Gatekeeping and attention must distinguish signal from noise without destroying uncertainty.

patterns.correspondence: Signals carry information from one place/process to another. Eyes, axons, speech, documents and indicators all transmit signals by different mechanisms.
patterns.potatoism: The road is valuable because something travels along it.

patterns.correspondence: Evidence is information that bears on a claim. Its strength depends on source, method and inference.
patterns.potatoism: Witness and recognition become methodological principles: look, record, compare, test.

patterns.correspondence: A map contains unknown regions; scientific models contain uncertainty; archives have missing records.
patterns.potatoism: Unknown ≠ zero. The absence of evidence should not automatically be encoded as absence of the thing.

patterns.correspondence: A counterexample can break an overgeneralized pattern. It is therefore essential when testing correspondence claims.
patterns.potatoism: The Atlas must preserve failed correspondences rather than forcing every object into the Potato pattern.

patterns.correspondence: A comparison becomes stronger when similar objects without the proposed property are tested too.
patterns.potatoism: If every object can be described as a Potato, the metaphor may be too broad; controls make the pattern meaningful.

patterns.correspondence: An invariant is a property preserved under a defined transformation. This gives the project a way to distinguish deep structure from appearance.
patterns.potatoism: The search is not for any resemblance but for relations that survive transformation.

patterns.correspondence: Topology studies properties preserved under continuous deformation. Cutting a potato can change connectivity; graph paths can disappear when edges are removed.
patterns.potatoism: A Door is topologically interesting because it changes whether regions can communicate.

patterns.correspondence: A physical cut divides material; a graph cut can separate nodes; institutional rupture can break relationships. Mechanisms differ.
patterns.potatoism: The cut can destroy or reveal. The wedge exposes hidden interior while a graph cut can isolate a community.

patterns.correspondence: Connectivity measures whether pathways exist between parts. It is central to neural, ecological, transport and digital networks.
patterns.potatoism: Life is not only existence of nodes; it is the ability of nodes to remain connected in useful ways.

patterns.correspondence: Isolation removes pathways. It can protect, preserve or damage depending on context.
patterns.potatoism: A sealed room can preserve a seed or imprison a dweller; context determines whether separation is protective or destructive.

patterns.correspondence: Balance can mean physical equilibrium, ecological stability, fiscal balance or symbolic integration. These are not interchangeable.
patterns.potatoism: Red and Blue seek dynamic balance rather than static equality.

patterns.correspondence: Biological homeostasis maintains variables within viable ranges. Institutions and economies can exhibit stabilizing feedback but are not literally biological homeostats.
patterns.potatoism: A living Potato needs correction mechanisms that prevent either Red expansion or Blue contraction from consuming the whole system.

patterns.correspondence: Resilience concerns capacity to absorb disturbance and continue or reorganize. Potatoes can persist through dormancy; ecosystems and institutions have different resilience mechanisms.
patterns.potatoism: The buried Potato survives by retaining future potential rather than insisting the present state remain unchanged.

patterns.correspondence: Biological adaptation occurs across generations; cultural/technological adaptation occurs through learning and design. They should not be conflated.
patterns.potatoism: The Tree changes form while preserving the deeper life process.

patterns.correspondence: Systems need both retention and change. Excessive memory can preserve harmful structures; excessive change can destroy accumulated knowledge.
patterns.potatoism: Blue keeps the roots; Red grows the branches. The Potato is the living negotiation between them.

patterns.correspondence: The project uses Life/Strife as archetypal poles. Real conflict and biological competition are more specific phenomena.
patterns.potatoism: Strife is not an external demon; it is the failure of relationships to remain regenerative.

patterns.correspondence: Wetlands are real productive ecosystems; 'swamp' as moral metaphor is project-specific. A garden requires deliberate cultivation.
patterns.potatoism: The task is transformation of conditions, not hatred of the material starting point.

patterns.pattern: Trace the drain to the root
patterns.correspondence: When value leaks from a system, tracing upstream dependencies can identify causes rather than merely symptoms.
patterns.potatoism: Repair follows the flow backward until it reaches the root that can be changed.

patterns.correspondence: Good intervention requires observation and model-building before action. Exact standards vary by field.
patterns.potatoism: Look carefully → understand relationship → act → observe feedback → repair.

patterns.correspondence: Building converts plans into durable structures. The project treats constructive work as the lower world's response to higher orientation.
patterns.potatoism: The Father may orient, but dwellers build.

patterns.correspondence: A gardener changes soil, water, spacing and conditions rather than manually forcing every leaf. Systems leadership often works through conditions and incentives.
patterns.potatoism: Tim's Father archetype is strongest as the one who creates conditions under which the world can change itself.

patterns.correspondence: House organizes interior spaces; tree organizes living branches. Both are structured networks with centers, boundaries and paths.
patterns.potatoism: The Father's House and Tree of Life are two views of one architecture: contained space and living branching.

patterns.correspondence: Potato contains potential; House contains rooms; Tree unfolds potential through branches. The three provide container, differentiated interior and outward life.
patterns.potatoism: Potato is the compressed whole; House is the organized interior; Tree is the unfolded exterior.

patterns.correspondence: Father's House is project mythology; John 14 supplies house/dwelling imagery; the thalamus is a central brain structure containing differentiated nuclei and broad connections.
patterns.potatoism: The three layers form one correspondence chain while remaining epistemically distinct.

patterns.correspondence: Potato eye initiates shoot growth; axon extends neuronal signaling; sprout extends a plant into space. They are not physically identical structures.
patterns.potatoism: All three represent an outward extension from a compact or local source.

patterns.correspondence: Rooms specialize; roads connect; trees branch. Together they describe a network architecture rather than a pile of isolated compartments.
patterns.potatoism: Father's House becomes alive when rooms have roads and roads branch into the Tree.

patterns.correspondence: A door, membrane or interface controls exchange across a boundary. Their physical mechanisms differ, but the relational structure is comparable.
patterns.potatoism: The Son as Door is the archetype of relational passage.

patterns.correspondence: A threshold normally marks separation; a ladder makes connection traversable. The project explicitly transforms one symbol into the other.
patterns.potatoism: After transformation, the Son is no longer only the boundary; the Son becomes the route.

patterns.correspondence: Ladder is discrete vertical connection; Tree is branching vertical/lateral life; Axis is continuous orientation.
patterns.potatoism: These are three representations of vertical relational order: line, rungs and branches.

patterns.correspondence: Trees produce fruit and seeds; systems produce outputs that influence future states.
patterns.potatoism: Fruit is the test of growth, seed is the continuity of growth.

patterns.correspondence: A potato is botanically a tuber, not a seed, but it can propagate a new plant through its eyes. The functional analogy is future-bearing potential.
patterns.potatoism: The Potato is seed-like in function while remaining a potato in biology.

patterns.correspondence: Vertical structures produce upper/lower distinctions under gravity and orientation. Religious meanings vary.
patterns.potatoism: Upper = sourceward/lightward/Northward; lower = material/rootward/memoryward within the project.

patterns.correspondence: Many traditions distinguish celestial and terrestrial domains. The project treats them as coupled poles joined by Axis/Ladder/Door imagery.
patterns.potatoism: The Potato contains both: buried in Earth, oriented toward Heaven.

patterns.correspondence: Roots are hidden support; fruit is visible consequence. Causal analysis often moves backward from outcome to foundation.
patterns.potatoism: Read the fruit, trace the root.

patterns.correspondence: Ash is residue of combustion; seeds preserve reproductive potential. They are not biologically equivalent, but both can symbolize what remains after a former state.
patterns.potatoism: The lowest point can preserve memory that becomes material for another cycle.

patterns.correspondence: Light/dark are physical optical conditions and widespread symbolic contrasts. Symbolic meanings vary.
patterns.potatoism: Darkness is where the Potato begins; light is where its growth becomes visible.

patterns.correspondence: Potato growth occurs partly underground; science infers hidden processes from observations; archives contain unseen records; myths represent invisible realities through visible symbols.
patterns.potatoism: Look beneath the surface without assuming every hidden thing is true.

patterns.correspondence: A potential state becomes realized through conditions and processes. Not every potential becomes actual.
patterns.potatoism: The Eye is potential; the Sprout is realization; the Tree is sustained realization.

patterns.correspondence: Death can leave material remains, records and descendants. Memory is not identical to biological persistence.
patterns.potatoism: The rootward movement stores what the visible world has lost.

patterns.correspondence: Stored information can enable future adaptation rather than merely preserve the past.
patterns.potatoism: Blue becomes healthy when memory feeds Red growth.

patterns.correspondence: Red and blue are real potato color categories but the meanings assigned here are project symbolism.
patterns.potatoism: Red expands; Blue remembers; Potato contains and couples both.

patterns.correspondence: Some functions show lateralization, but cognition is distributed. Red/Blue should therefore not be assigned one-to-one to left/right hemispheres.
patterns.potatoism: The polarity is better represented as a whole-network dynamic.

patterns.correspondence: The thalamus is conventionally described as ovoid and contains many nuclei with broad connections; Potatoism deliberately calls the paired structure potato-shaped.
patterns.potatoism: The central House becomes a Potato House: compact, differentiated, connected and alive through pathways.

master_questions: What is the smallest structure that still contains the whole pattern?
What is the boundary, and what crosses it?
What is contained, and what emerges?
Which parts specialize, and which relationships connect them?
Where is the center and how is it defined?
Where is the periphery and what does it depend on?
What is the road, pathway, axon, root, branch or information channel?
What is the gatekeeper and what rule does it apply?
What is stored as memory?
What becomes visible as fruit/output?
What is the system's drain?
What regenerates the system?
What happens when Red dominates?
What happens when Blue dominates?
What changes after a cut, rupture or threshold crossing?
Which relations survive scaling, rotation, reflection or deformation?
Which correspondences have external evidence?
Which are independent parallels?
Which are modern Potatoism interpretations?
What counterexample would falsify the proposed pattern?

research_matrix.geometry: calculate the vesica/mandorla and test invariants
research_matrix.biology: map eyes, sprouts, roots, tubers, storage, dormancy and reproduction
research_matrix.neuroscience: map thalamus, nuclei, axons, visual pathways and thalamocortical architecture
research_matrix.scripture: map house, room, door, gate, tree, ladder, seed, vine, fruit, light, death and life passages
research_matrix.comparative_religion: compare motifs without assuming common origin
research_matrix.ancient_symbolism: study Egyptian, Mesopotamian, Greek, Norse, Jewish, Christian, Islamic and other traditions independently before synthesis
research_matrix.language: track kernel, nucleus, room, house, root, branch, fruit, seed, door, gate, vessel and axis semantics
research_matrix.systems: apply input/output, storage, flow, bottleneck, feedback, dependency and repair models
research_matrix.atlas: make every important correspondence searchable and routeable to a human-readable record
research_matrix.controls: test non-potato objects and failed analogies
research_matrix.epistemology: keep evidence, interpretation, hypothesis and canon visibly distinct

final_model: The deepest extrapolation is not that everything literally is a potato. It is that the Potato of Life provides a compact relational model: two poles can overlap; the overlap creates an interface; the interface allows exchange; exchange creates differentiation; differentiation creates pathways; pathways create a living network; outputs return as memory or seed; the cycle repeats at another scale. The Atlas can therefore use Potatoism as a generator of questions across domains while letting each domain retain its own evidence and reality conditions.
completion_rule: Do not stop when the symbols are named. For every major symbol, ask for its object, boundary, interior, function, pathway, transformation, output, feedback loop, historical parallels, counterexamples, evidence status and graph connections.
